rows.journey: I am a B.Com student, CFA Program Candidate, and entrepreneur, currently building my journey toward a career in finance while running a home bakery business alongside my studies. But before I became interested in finance, entrepreneurship, or the markets, there was a school that helped shape the person I am today. I am a proud alumnus of Shree Siddhi Vinayagar English High School, from the 2021–22 batch. When I look back at my school years, I realise that many of the qualities I rely on today were not learned from a textbook. One of the most meaningful parts of my school journey was training in martial arts under Akshay Sir and eventually earning my Black Belt. The Black Belt was never just a designation for me. The real achievement was everything it taught me along the way — discipline when I didn't feel motivated, consistency when progress was slow, patience when things didn't happen immediately, and the habit of showing up and doing the work. Those lessons stayed with me long after I left school. I am deeply grateful to Akshay Sir for being an important mentor in that journey, and to every teacher and mentor who, in their own way, contributed to the person I am becoming. Some lessons from school are remembered as chapters in a textbook; others quietly become part of your character. I believe mine did the latter. After school, I chose Commerce and began my journey at Ramniranjan Jhunjhunwala College, University of Mumbai. Over time, I developed a strong interest in finance, financial markets, investing and understanding how businesses and capital work. That curiosity eventually led me toward the CFA Program. Today, I am studying areas such as equity analysis, portfolio management, corporate finance, investment analysis and professional ethics—not simply to pass an examination, but because I genuinely want to understand how the financial world works. At the same time, I have been building something completely different from my finance journey: my own home bakery business. Starting a business from home has taught me lessons that no classroom could fully teach me—how to understand customers, manage costs, maintain quality, deal with uncertainty, take responsibility when things go wrong, and keep improving when nobody is forcing you to. My journey has also had its share of difficult setbacks and challenges. There have been moments when life tested me physically, mentally and emotionally. But if there is one thing I have learned from all of it, it is this: **You may not always control what happens to you, but you can decide whether you will stand back up.** The discipline I learned through martial arts, the curiosity I developed through education, the courage required to build a business, and the resilience developed through difficult moments are all becoming part of the professional I am trying to build. I am still learning. Still making mistakes. Still figuring things out. And I don't want to pretend otherwise. My goal is not simply to collect qualifications or titles. I want to become someone who combines financial knowledge with discipline, entrepreneurial thinking, integrity and the ability to create meaningful value for others. I also document my journey through my **Student → Analyst** series, sharing what I learn about finance, investing and professional development in the hope that someone else can learn alongside me. And wherever my career takes me, I want to remain connected to where my journey began. I don't see my school as just a place I attended between certain years. It is one of the places that helped shape who I became. I hope that as I grow, I can return not only as an alumnus, but as someone who can contribute—by mentoring students, sharing what I have learned, creating awareness about careers and financial literacy, and helping the next generation believe that their starting point does not have to define their destination. **Forever grateful for the teachers, mentors, friends and experiences that helped shape my foundation.** **Still learning. Still building. Still becoming.**
